TASK: The assembler was seating connector housings into the fixture at final assembly station 6. The task was underway because this is the normal running work at this station for the whole shift. Stage of the task: in process - normal running work. Procedure reference not determined at time of report: the station standard work number is being confirmed by the area lead. The task was being performed as written. Equipment involved: Final assembly fixture at station 6. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: The fixture was replaced about six weeks ago and sits roughly 4 inches further forward than the previous one. Object handled weighed approximately 4 ounces per connector housing. Object size and shape: about 2 inches square, gripped between the thumb and first two fingers. The object was held as follows: pinch grip between the thumb and the first two fingers of the right hand, with a bare hand for feel. PPE in use: Safety glasses only, gloves are not worn at this station because they reduce feel. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: The task is performed approximately 300 units per shift. The assembler has performed this task for about 14 months on this station. One cycle of the task consists of the following: reach forward about 20 inches into the bin, grasp the housing in a pinch grip, rotate the right wrist about 90 degrees to line it up with the fixture, press down with the heel of the hand to seat it, then release and return to the bin. Force and posture required: about 6 pounds of downward press per unit with the right wrist bent back and rotated, held about 20 inches forward of the body. Symptom onset: Aching and tingling in the right wrist first noticed about eight weeks ago, at first only in the last hour of a shift. Symptom progression: Now present through most of the shift and waking the employee at night, and grip strength has dropped when lifting trays at home. Recent change in the work: The fixture was replaced about six weeks ago and sits roughly 4 inches further forward, so the reach and the wrist rotation are both greater than before.

MECHANISM: Motion involved: Right wrist rotation of about 90 degrees with the wrist bent back, combined with a downward press using the heel of the hand. Repetition: four wrist rotations per unit, about 300 units per shift. Force and posture: About 6 pounds of press force per repetition with the wrist bent back and the arm extended about 20 inches forward.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The fixture change six weeks ago increased the reach and the wrist rotation, and the station has not been reassessed since. Conditions at the point of injury: nothing notable about the environment. Timing: Symptoms are worst in the last two hours of an 8 hour shift, with about one overtime shift a week. The assembler had performed this task before. Whether a known hazard or prior action covers this task was not determined at time of report. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity not determined at time of report: there was no single event at which work could have been stopped.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: First aid at the scene: No first aid was given because the condition was reported at the end of a shift rather than at the time. No first aid was given at the scene. Notification: The team lead was told at the end of the shift and EHS the following morning. Reason for the delay in reporting: the tingling was mild at first and was expected to settle, and reporting it would have meant stopping the line. Scene and equipment: Nothing was secured because there was no single event or scene to preserve. Work at the location continued in a modified way. The assembler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
